headline: MacKinnon (lower-body) will play in Game 4 in Vegas.
news: MacKinnon left Game Three on Sunday late in the second period after suffering a lower-body injury. He returned early in the third period, but was used sparingly, spending most of the final frame on the bench. It's unclear if he will be able to return to his usual playing capacity in Game Four, but his presence will nevertheless be a positive sign for an Avalanche team trying to stave off elimination.

headline: Kaprizov (undisclosed) will play Sunday vs. the Blue Jackets.
Guentzel (rest) will not play against the Rangers on Wednesday.
Nylander (illness) is on the ice for warmups; he's expected to play vs. the Sharks.
Oettinger will start vs. Winnipeg on Thursday.
news: The Stars have struggled offensively at times to start the season, but they can point to Jake Oettinger's outstanding play as the reason for their 5-3-1 record. In seven games this season (4-2-1), the 27-year-old Oettinger has already posted three shutouts, with an outstanding 1.13 GAA and .945 SV%. He saved 18 of 20 shots (.900 SV%) in his previous game, a 3-2 overtime win over the Boston Bruins. The Stars enter Thursday's divisional clash as sizeable -196 home favourites against a Winnipeg Jets team that has scored two or fewer goals in three of their last five games (1-3-1).

headline: Schaefer (illness) will play vs. New Jersey on Tuesday.
news: Schaefer was absent from practice on Monday due to illness, but he attended the team's morning skate on Tuesday and will be in the lineup in the evening against the New Jersey Devils. The 18-year-old rookie's tremendous season continued in the Islanders' most recent game, recording two goals, including the overtime winner, in a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs. He has 28 points (12G / 16A) in 42 games this season.

headline: Marner (personal) will not play Thursday in St. Louis.
Bedard (shoulder) is expected to make his season debut vs. Pittsburgh on Tuesday.
news: Bedard missed all of training camp and the opening six games of the season, but he should make his debut on Tuesday against the Pittsburgh Penguins. The Blackhawks can't afford to go much longer without their 21-year-old superstar after scoring just 12 goals in their first six games (1-5-0). Bedard had 30 goals, 75 points and 226 SOG in 69 GP last season.

headline: Heiskanen (lower-body) will play in Game 1 vs. Minnesota.
news: Heiskanen missed the final three games of the regular season with a lower-body injury, but was a full participant in Friday's practice and will play in Game 1 on Saturday. Heiskanen had another incredible season, posting nine goals and 54 assists (63 points) in 77 games.

headline: Point (rest) will not play against the Rangers on Wednesday.
Bobrovsky will start vs. New York on Thursday.
news: The Maple Leafs are riding their first winning streak of the season and hope to extend it to three games on Thursday against the New York Rangers, with Bobrovsky between the pipes. The 38-year-old Bobrovsky has had an up-and-down start with the Maple Leafs, but he's coming off a tremendous performance, stopping 30 of 31 shots (.968 SV%) in a 3-1 win over the San Jose Sharks. He has a 2.96 GAA and .902 SV% in seven games (2-3-2). The Maple Leafs enter Thursday's contest as slight -104 home underdogs against a surprising 7-3-1 Rangers team.

headline: 2-year, $18,000,000 contract with the Vegas Golden Knights. Breakdown to be confirmed . Expires 2029 (UFA).
Smith (upper-body) will return in Detroit on Friday.
news: Smith has not played in over a month, but has ramped things up over the last week after returning to contact drills in practice, and could return to the lineup as soon on Friday against the Detroit Red Wings. The 20-year-old second-year player has 29 points (12G / 17A) in 33 games this season.

headline: Blake (rest) is expected to be back in the Hurricanes' lineup on Monday.
news: With Carolina locking up their playoff position over the weekend, Jackson Blake found himself out of the lineup due to rest related purposes but will draw back into the lineup vs. Philadelphia on Monday. The 22-year-old forward has taken a massive step forward in his second NHL season, picking up career highs in goals (22), assists (30), points (52), PIMs (40) and SOG (167) through 79 games played.

headline: Podkolzin (illness) will play vs. Philadelphia on Saturday.
Dunn (upper-body) is out vs. Los Angeles on Tuesday.
news: Dunn exited Monday's 3-1 win over the Anaheim Ducks after only 15:14 time-on-ice due to an undisclosed injury. The 29-year-old defenseman has 19 points (5G / 14A) in 34 games this season. With Brandon Montour (hand) also out of the lineup, Seattle will be thin on the blueline in Tuesday's game against the Los Angeles Kings.

headline: Lafreniere (illness) is expected to play vs. Buffalo on Thursday.
news: The Rangers are battling a myriad of key injuries and had a scare on Wednesday when Lafreneiere was absent from practice because of an illness, but he should play on Thursday against the Buffalo Sabres. The 24-year-old Lafreniere has been held off the scoresheet in 28 of 44 games this season and continues to be unable to live up to the expectations he garnered when he was drafted first overall in the 2020 NHL Entry Draft. He has 24 points (9G / 15A) in 44 games this season.

headline: Stankoven (illness) missed practice on Thursday.
news: Stankoven is battling an illness and did not practice on Thursday, but will be hopeful to play when Carolina opens the postseason on Saturday. Stankoven has been an effective offensive contributor in his previous two postseasons and hopes to carry his late-season momentum into a deep playoff run for the Hurricanes. The 23-year-old has nine points (7G / 2A) during a six-game point streak.

headline: Wedgewood will start in New Jersey on Tuesday.
news: Wedgewood's tremendous 2025-26 season, posting a 2.02 GAA and .921 SV% in 45 appearances (31-6-6), should at least earn him a near timeshare by season's end, but Colorado has leaned heavily on Mackenzie Blackwood to start the 2026-27 season. That said, Wedgewood will tend the twine on Tuesday in the tail end of a back-to-back, his third start in 10 games this season. The 34-year-old Wedgewood has a 2.40 GAA and .902 SV% in two games (1-0-1). Colorado enters Tuesday's action as slight +100 road underdogs against a New Jersey Devils team coming off a 4-2 loss to the Washington Capitals.

headline: Jarry will start vs. Toronto on Saturday.
